Afonso: Portuguese form of Alphonse, from Germanic Adalfuns, 'noble and ready'. Borne by the first king of Portugal.
Emmi: Finnish and German pet form of Emma, from Germanic ermen 'whole, universal'.
Lilo: Probably a short form of Liselotte or Lieselotte (German), or the Hawaiian lilo 'lost, generous'. Origin uncertain.
Qasim: Arabic, 'one who divides or distributes'. Name of a son of the Prophet Muhammad.
Halimatou: West African (Fula, French spelling) form of Arabic Halima, 'gentle, patient'.
Boran: Turkish, meaning 'storm' or 'thunderstorm'. Also used in Balkan and Slavic contexts; origin varies.
Izabella: Hungarian, Polish and Slavic form of Isabella, a Spanish form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Mateus: Portuguese form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Pipa: Probably a short form of Philippa, feminine of Philip, Greek 'lover of horses'. Also a Spanish nickname.
Clarysse: French-style variant of Clarice or Clarissa, from Latin clarus 'bright, famous'.
Zayed: Arabic Zayd, 'growth, abundance'. Famous through Sheikh Zayed of the United Arab Emirates.
Darwin: English surname, from Old English deore wine 'dear friend'. Made famous by naturalist Charles Darwin.
Ube: Frisian name, probably a short form of Germanic names with ub-, 'wolf' or 'fury'. Origin uncertain.
Zyon: Modern spelling of Zion, Hebrew for the hill of Jerusalem; used as a name meaning 'highest point' or 'sign'.
Baya: Arabic and Berber name, possibly 'sweet scent' or related to Hebrew Beya. Origin uncertain.
Jaad: Probably a variant of Arabic Jad, 'generous', or of Jaad as a modern coined spelling. Origin uncertain.
Nya: Probably African or modern coined; in Swahili nya can relate to 'purpose'. Origin uncertain.
Adélia: Portuguese form of Adèle, from Germanic adal 'noble'.
Rehan: Arabic Rayhan, 'sweet basil, fragrant plant'; also used in South Asia.
Rozan: Probably Kurdish or Arabic, linked to 'rose' or 'window' (rozan in Persian). Origin uncertain.
Dayna: Modern English variant of Dana, possibly 'from Denmark' or Hebrew-linked 'judge'. Origin uncertain.
Hayk: Armenian, from Hayk, the legendary founder of the Armenian nation.
Saleh: Arabic, 'righteous, virtuous, good'. Name of a prophet in the Quran.
Noar: Probably a variant of Noor or Hebrew na'ar 'youth, boy'. Origin uncertain.
Thya: Probably a modern coined form, perhaps from Greek Thea 'goddess' or a variant of Tia. Origin uncertain.
Fidel: Spanish and French, from Latin fidelis 'faithful'.
Maylan: Modern coined name, blending May and the suffix -lan; possibly from Chinese-influenced Mei-lan 'plum orchid'. Origin uncertain.
Roma: Italian name of the city Rome, of uncertain origin; also a Slavic short form of Romana.
Ayza: Probably a variant of Aisha or Aiza, Arabic-related 'alive, living'. Origin uncertain.
Siara: Probably a modern variant of Sierra or Ciara; possibly Irish 'dark one'. Origin uncertain.
Livy: English pet form of Olivia or Livia, from Latin oliva 'olive' or Roman clan name Livius.
Arkan: Arabic, 'pillars' or 'foundations'; also found in Turkic and Kurdish usage.
Artin: Armenian and Persian name; in Armenian possibly from Ardin, 'earnest' or 'righteous'. Origin uncertain.
Ayanna: Probably African-American coinage; possibly from Swahili or Hebrew, 'beautiful flower'. Origin uncertain.
Iustin: Romanian form of Justin, from Latin iustus 'just, fair'.
Élisa: French form of Elisa, short for Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Sayed: Arabic Sayyid, 'master, lord'; a title of respect used as a name.
Cosmo: Italian form of Cosmas, from Greek kosmos 'order, universe, beauty'.
Ibrahiem: Variant spelling of Ibrahim, the Arabic form of Abraham, 'father of many'.
Tiam: Probably a variant of Tiamat or a modern coined name; may also be Persian or Vietnamese. Origin uncertain.
Azer: Turkic and Persian, from azar 'fire'; also Hebrew Azer 'helper'. Origin varies.
Saga: Old Norse, 'story' or 'tale'; also the name of a Norse goddess.
Arel: Hebrew, 'lion of God' or 'angel'. Used in Jewish and Turkish contexts.
Élia: French form of Elia or Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Also used as a feminine name.
Célou: Probably a French pet form of Célia or Marcel. Origin uncertain.
Siya: Sanskrit and Hindi, 'Sita' form; also Zulu 'we are going'. Origin varies.
Shloimy: Yiddish pet form of Shloime, the Yiddish form of Solomon, Hebrew 'peace'.
Remon: Dutch form of Raymond, from Germanic ragin 'counsel' and mund 'protector'.
Elianna: Modern blend of Eli or Elia and Anna; Hebrew 'my God has answered' with 'grace'.
Swann: French spelling of Swan, from Old English swan, or Germanic Swan- names. Also literary (Proust).
Léano: Probably a modern coinage, perhaps from Leo or Leandro. Origin uncertain.
Love: Swedish name, from Old Norse Leifr 'heir' or from the English word. As girls' name, the word 'love'.
Líon: Probably a variant of Lion or Irish lion 'fierce'. Origin uncertain.
Yaqub: Arabic form of Jacob, Hebrew 'supplanter' or 'may God protect'.
Yusef: Arabic Yusuf, the form of Joseph, Hebrew 'God will add'.
Loën: Probably a modern Breton or French coinage, perhaps from Loïc or Leon. Origin uncertain.
Marla: English, a short form of Marlene or Mary-related names; Marlene blends Maria and Magdalena.
Saule: Lithuanian and Latvian, meaning 'sun'; also a French form of Saul, Hebrew 'asked for'.
Vieve: Short form of Genevieve, from Germanic or Celtic roots, possibly 'woman of the race'.
Aser: Spanish form of Asher, Hebrew 'happy, blessed'.
Raph: Short form of Raphaël, Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Artis: Latvian male name, a form of Arthur or Artūrs; or English surname-based. Origin uncertain.
Ivaan: Variant spelling of Ivan, Slavic form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Manisa: Turkish city name, possibly of Greek origin from Magnesia; also used in Thai as 'sweet'. Origin uncertain.
Yafa: Hebrew, 'beautiful', same as Yaffa or Jaffa.
Mondo: Probably a short form of Edmondo or Raimondo; also Italian for 'world'.
Noéli: Variant of Noëlle, French feminine of Noël, from Latin natalis 'birth', meaning Christmas.
Osaid: Arabic Usayd, 'little lion' or 'ardent'; diminutive of asad 'lion'.
Lilibeth: English compound of Lili and Beth, both from Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Ossaïd: French spelling of Arabic Usayd, 'little lion'.
Nick: English short form of Nicholas, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Christopher: Greek, 'bearer of Christ'. Saint Christopher is the patron of travellers.
Nathalie: French form of Natalia, from Latin natalis 'birthday', meaning Christmas.
Laurie: English and French diminutive of Laurence or Laura, from Latin laurus 'laurel'.
Larissa: Greek, probably 'citadel'; the name of a Greek city. Also possibly linked to a Russian 'seagull'.
Bent: Danish and Dutch short form of Benedict, from Latin 'blessed'.
Benoît: French form of Benedict, from Latin benedictus 'blessed'.
Oussama: Arabic Usama, 'lion'. Common spelling in the French-speaking Maghreb.
Samantha: English, possibly from Aramaic 'listener' or a blend of Samuel and the Greek anthos 'flower'. Origin uncertain.
Heleen: Dutch form of Helen, from Greek helene, possibly 'torch' or 'shining light'.
Marouane: French spelling of Arabic Marwan, possibly 'flint' or 'strong stone'.
Anouck: Dutch and French pet form of Anna, Hebrew 'grace'.
Rens: Dutch short form of Laurens or Renier, from Latin Laurentius 'of Laurentum' or Germanic 'counsel'.
Emelie: Swedish and Dutch form of Emily, from Latin Aemilia, a Roman clan name.
Megan: Welsh pet form of Margaret, from Greek margarites 'pearl'.
Enya: Irish, from Eithne 'kernel, grain'; also spelled Enya by the singer.
Zineb: Arabic Zaynab, 'fragrant tree' or 'father's jewel'. A daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.
Maïlys: French, a blend of Maï (May) and Lys 'lily', possibly a modern Breton-influenced coinage.
Arnout: Dutch form of Arnold, from Germanic arn 'eagle' and wald 'rule'.
Ayrton: English surname, from places in Yorkshire meaning 'settlement on the River Aire'. Popularised by Ayrton Senna.
Inez: Spanish and Portuguese form of Agnes, from Greek hagne 'pure, holy'.
Youness: Arabic Yunus, the form of Jonah, Hebrew 'dove'.
Laïs: Greek, the name of famous courtesans of Corinth; meaning uncertain, possibly 'popular'.
Candice: English, from Candace, the title of Ethiopian queens; possibly Greek-Latin 'glowing white'.
Michèle: French feminine of Michel, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Thorben: Scandinavian and German, from Old Norse Thorbjörn, 'Thor's bear'.
Antony: English variant of Anthony, from the Roman clan name Antonius, of uncertain meaning.
Emmeline: French and English, from Germanic amal 'work' or erm 'whole'. Related to Emma.
Auriane: French, probably from Latin aurum 'gold' or a modern blend with Ariane. Origin uncertain.
Ylana: Probably a variant of Ilana, Hebrew 'tree', or a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Lani: Hawaiian, 'sky' or 'heaven'; also a short form of names like Leilani.
Lori: English short form of Laura or Lorraine; also a Hungarian form of Laura.
Hakan: Turkish and Scandinavian; in Turkish from khagan 'ruler, emperor'.
Louanne: French or English compound of Lou (Louise) and Anne.
Souhaila: Arabic, feminine of Suhail, 'smooth, easy'; also a star name.
Abderrahmane: Arabic Abd al-Rahman, 'servant of the Merciful'.
Nando: Short form of Fernando, Germanic 'bold journey' or 'brave voyager'.
Redouan: French spelling of Arabic Ridwan, 'good pleasure, contentment'.
Ewan: Scottish and Welsh form of Eoghan, possibly 'born of the yew' or 'youth'.
Neel: Hindi and Sanskrit, 'blue'; in Dutch also a short form of Cornelis or Daniel.
Yoann: French form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Sephora: French form of Zipporah, Hebrew 'bird'. The wife of Moses.
Kemal: Turkish, from Arabic kamal 'perfection, maturity'. Associated with Atatürk.
Riccardo: Italian form of Richard, Germanic 'brave ruler'.
Rihanna: Probably from Arabic Rayhana, 'sweet basil'. Popularised by the Barbadian singer.
Ilenia: Italian, probably a variant of Ilaria or from Greek-linked Helen. Origin uncertain.
Alisha: Variant of Alicia or Alisa, ultimately from Germanic Adalheid 'noble kind'.
Rein: Dutch short form of Reinier or Reinhard, Germanic 'counsel' and 'brave'.
Sergio: Italian and Spanish form of Sergius, a Roman clan name of uncertain meaning.
Franne: Probably a Dutch or Flemish variant of Frannie, from Frances, 'free one' or 'Frenchman'.
Loewie: Probably a Flemish pet form of Lowie or Lodewijk, Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Roberto: Italian and Spanish form of Robert, Germanic 'bright fame'.
Sally: English pet form of Sarah, Hebrew 'princess'.
Mustapha: Arabic Mustafa, 'the chosen one'; a title of the Prophet Muhammad.
Pim: Dutch short form of Willem, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'; also a pet form of Pieter.
Elizan: Probably a modern blend of Eliza and Ann, or Kurdish. Origin uncertain.
Loriana: Italian, a blend of Lori or Laura with Ana, from Latin laurus 'laurel'. Probably a modern coinage.
Imme: Dutch and Frisian, a short form of Germanic names with irmin 'whole, great', such as Imke.
Suzy: English pet form of Susan, from Hebrew shoshanna 'lily'.
Belle: French, 'beautiful'; also a short form of Isabelle.
Berra: Probably Turkish Berra, 'pious, righteous'; from Arabic barr. Origin uncertain.
Briana: Feminine of Brian, probably Celtic 'high, noble'.
Alistair: Scottish form of Alexander, Greek 'defender of men'.
Veronica: From Latin and Greek, 'bringer of victory' or 'true image'. Saint Veronica wiped Christ's face.
Jesper: Danish and Dutch form of Jasper, probably from Persian 'treasurer'; one of the Magi.
Elinor: English form of Eleanor, possibly from Provençal Aliénor, of uncertain origin.
May: English, from the month of May or a short form of Mary or Margaret.
Maëlia: Modern French, probably from Breton Maël 'prince' with a feminine ending. Origin uncertain.
Danilo: Slavic and Italian form of Daniel, Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Silvia: Latin, 'of the forest'. Mother of Romulus and Remus was Rhea Silvia.
Denisa: Slavic and Romanian feminine of Dennis, from Greek Dionysios, god of wine.
Mélyna: Modern French variant of Melina, from Greek meli 'honey'. Origin partly uncertain.
Obi: Igbo (Nigerian), 'heart'; also short form of Obinna.
Mayssae: Variant of Arabic Maysa, Maysaa, 'proud, swaying walk'.
Lorian: Probably a modern coinage from Lorenzo or Lorraine. Origin uncertain.
Féliz: Spanish-influenced spelling of Felix or Feliz, Latin 'happy, lucky'.
Paulina: Latin, feminine diminutive of Paulus 'small, humble'.
Ena: Irish form of Eithne 'kernel', or Spanish short form of names ending -ena. Also Croatian pet form of Jelena.
Yseult: Medieval Welsh-Cornish legend, Isolde; meaning uncertain, possibly 'fair one'.
Antonina: Latin, feminine of Antoninus, from the Roman clan Antonius.
Luíz: Portuguese variant of Luiz or Luís, from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Tino: Italian short form of names ending in -tino, such as Valentino or Costantino.
Mikaïl: Arabic and French form of Michael, Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Natéo: Modern French coinage, probably blending Nathan or Théo. Origin uncertain.
Malin: Swedish short form of Magdalena, 'woman of Magdala'; also Dutch Malin variants.
Abygaëlle: Variant of Abigail, Hebrew 'my father is joy'.
Anna-Maria: Compound of Anna (Hebrew 'grace') and Maria (Hebrew, possibly 'beloved' or 'bitter').
Felice: Italian, from Latin felix 'happy, lucky'; used for both sexes.
Maïmouna: West African form of Arabic Maymuna, 'blessed, fortunate'.
Bess: English short form of Elizabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Loélia: Modern French coinage; possibly combining Loé or Lou with Célia. Origin uncertain.
Elano: Probably a modern coinage or variant of Eliano, from Latin Aelianus. Origin uncertain.
Aubane: Probably a French variant of Alban or Aubin, from Latin albus 'white'.
Malick: West African form of Arabic Malik, 'king'.
Tibbe: Frisian and Dutch short form of Tiebert or Theodebert, Germanic 'people bright'. Probably.
Dino: Italian short form of names such as Bernardino or Edoardo.
Damiano: Italian form of Damian, Greek damazo 'to tame'.
Lény: French variant of Lenny or Léon, from Greek leon 'lion'. Probably.
Nelis: Dutch short form of Cornelis, from Latin Cornelius, perhaps 'horn'.
Thyago: Brazilian spelling of Tiago, Portuguese form of James, from Hebrew Jacob 'supplanter'.
Mari: Welsh, Finnish and Scandinavian form of Mary, from Hebrew, possibly 'beloved' or 'bitter'.
